intervals.label: seafloor installation begins
intervals.note: Site-wide KM3NeT installation start; no source consulted (checked 2026-09-17) gives a separate ARCA-specific first-string date.
intervals.quote: In the early morning of 3 December 2015, scientists and engineers started the installation of KM3NeT

intervals.label: initial core operational (6 detection units)
intervals.note: Marks the point at which ARCA is described by the collaboration as having an operating 'initial core'. Physics data-taking with partial arrays (ARCA6, ARCA8, ARCA19, ARCA21, etc.) has continued and grown since; this interval is left open (end: null) because ARCA is still being extended, not because the 6-DU configuration itself persists.
intervals.quote: six detection units are now in operation, representing the initial core of the KM3NeT/ARCA neutrino telescope

intervals.label: 51 detection units operating (current, undated official statement)
intervals.note: The source page carries no publication or last-updated date; 'start' is set to the year the page was read (2026) as a lower bound only, not a claim that 51 detection units were reached exactly in 2026. It is recorded as the most detailed available snapshot of construction progress; the precise date is uncertain.
intervals.quote: Currently the ARCA detector is operated with 51 detection units.

name: KM3NeT/ARCA
notes: sensor_count (total optical-module or PMT count) is left unset: the LoI states 18 optical modules per string and 31 PMTs per optical module, but no source consulted states a total ARCA-wide optical-module or PMT count directly, and multiplying per-string figures by the design string count would be an unsourced derived computation.
depth_min (top of the instrumented array) is left unset for the same reason: the LoI states a ~700 m detection-unit height but no source states the resulting top-of-array depth directly.

placements.note: This 2015-12-03 news item describes the start of KM3NeT seafloor installation generally; it is used here as the start of ARCA's placement at Capo Passero because the KM3NeT-It / Capo Passero site is where the described installation infrastructure was laid. No official page consulted (checked 2026-09-17) names a distinct 'first ARCA detection unit online' date; the earliest ARCA-specific operational milestone sourced is the six-detection-unit announcement of 2021-04-15 (see intervals).
placements.quote: In the early morning of 3 December 2015, scientists and engineers started the installation of KM3NeT, which once completed, will be largest detector of neutrinos in the Northern Hemisphere.

depth_max.note: Seabed anchor depth of the ARCA site, i.e. the maximum depth of the detector.
depth_max.quote: At a depth of about 3500 m

instrumented_volume.display: ~1 km3 (design, two building blocks of 115 detection units each)
instrumented_volume.note: Design (final) instrumented volume when both building blocks (230 detection units total) are complete; only a fraction of the detection units are deployed as of 2026 (see intervals).
instrumented_volume.quote: instrumented volume of ARCA is about 1 cubic kilometer in two 'building blocks' of 115 detection units each

string_count.display: 230 detection units (design: two building blocks of 115 each)
string_count.note: Derived: 230 = 2 building blocks x 115 detection units each (both numbers are in the quote). Design total. As of the 2026 access date, the official 'Astroparticle physics with ARCA' page states 51 detection units are actually operating (see intervals); that as-built figure is not repeated here as the spec value to avoid conflating design capacity with current construction state.
string_count.quote: instrumented volume of ARCA is about 1 cubic kilometer in two 'building blocks' of 115 detection units each

summary.plain: The bigger of the two KM3NeT telescopes, built for spotting very high-energy neutrinos from deep space. It sits 3500 metres down on the seabed off Sicily and, when finished, will fill about a cubic kilometre of seawater with light sensors.
summary.technical: KM3NeT/ARCA (Astroparticle Research with Cosmics in the Abyss): sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope at the KM3NeT-It site off Capo Passero, Sicily (3500 m depth), designed as two building blocks of 115 detection units each (~1 km3 instrumented volume) for high-energy astrophysical neutrino detection; 51 detection units were operating as of the 2026 access date, with construction ongoing.

technology.locator: Letter of Intent for KM3NeT 2.0, abstract
technology.quote: each optical module comprises 31 photo-multiplier tubes (PMTs). Each building block thus constitutes a 3-dimensional array of photo sensors that can be used to detect the Cherenkov light produced by relativistic particles emerging from neutrino interactions.
technology.value: Sea-water Cherenkov neutrino telescope: vertical strings of digital optical modules, each housing photomultiplier tubes, anchored to the Mediterranean seabed
